extracted.intended_audience: museum professionals and prospective Museums for America (MFA) applicants (museum directors, grant writers, program staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for preparing and understanding Museums for America (MFA) grant applications and for how MFA projects are categorized, implemented, and assessed. Includes grant category definitions, allowable activities, application/process requirements, and observed patterns that affect funding likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging Communities (Education, Exhibitions, and Interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: This category encompasses the broadest range possible of educational activities by which museums share collections, content, and knowledge to support learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects may include, but are not limited to: classes and presentations; creation of digital content for programmatic purposes; curricula development; exhibition design/fabrication; exhibition development/implementation; integration of technology; interpretive strategies; programming and education for Adults, Families, Underserved communities, Youth (pre-K through grade 12); public programs; publications; research for program/exhibit development; web site content and design. The category is broad and is where the largest number of applications were submitted after the 2008 category change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building Institutional Capacity (Management, Policy, and Training)
rubrics_metrics.description: This category supports projects and activities that serve to improve the infrastructure of museums to better serve their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects may include, but are not limited to: financial management; personnel administration; planning (institutional, maintenance, emergency/disaster); policy development; staff training and development; technology enhancements. Emphasizes strengthening institutional operations and capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections Stewardship (Management of Collections)
rubrics_metrics.description: This category supports activities museums undertake to maintain and improve the management of museum collections in order to fulfill the museum’s public service mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects may include: collections planning; collections security and safety; database development/enhancements; digitization of collections; mapping for living plant collections (not surveys); registration/cataloguing; research/documentation; risk assessment. Typically serves collections-based institutions and may involve minimal or no direct audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to articulate strategic role and alignment with mission/long-range plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must articulate the strategic role of a proposed project in terms of their core mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MFA funds projects with the potential to support museums' ability to advance goals and objectives of their long-range plans and to grow as institutions. Applications should clearly frame projects in terms of institutional needs and strategic goals; reviewers and evaluation emphasize mission alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory 1:1 cost sharing requirement (match)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1:1 cost sharing requirement is mandated by statute for MFA awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This match requirement can pose an obstacle for small museums and should be planned for in budgets. Applicants must account for eligible matching funds and demonstrate ability to meet statutory match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission via grants.gov (submission process requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2008, MFA applications must be submitted electronically through grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The switch to grants.gov introduced technical demands (downloading, entering, and submitting online forms) that deterred some museums unfamiliar with the process. Applicants should ensure technical capacity and staff knowledge to complete electronic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary activity area classification (resource-allocation basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should identify a primary activity area defined by the area of greatest resource allocation: Programming, Exhibitions, Digitization/Collections, Technology/Online resources, or Organizational Development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation and reporting use this classification to characterize projects. Applicants should state which activity area will receive the greatest share of resources and justify budget allocation accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable project activities (49 activity list; examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: MFA projects may comprise many specific activities (survey presented a 49-item list); allowable activities span programming, organizational development, exhibitions, technology, and collections/digitization work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common programming activities (examples and prevalence): educational programming (e.g., develop on-site education programs — 84% of programming projects), general programming (e.g., interpretive programs, demonstrations, workshops), broadcast/live programming. Other activities include creating curriculum guides, in-school education programs, internships/mentoring/apprenticeships, training sessions, conferences, website development, purchasing equipment, research/evaluation, hiring consultants, staff training, database development, digitization, registration/cataloguing, mapping living plant collections, and risk assessment. Applicants may (and often do) select multiple activities; be explicit about each activity proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of multi-activity projects and breadth of activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Most MFA projects span several activity areas and include multiple distinct activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 85% of projects spanned several areas; over a third entailed four to six activity areas; average project conducted ~12 different activities (range 1–41). Applicants should design projects anticipating cross-over activities (e.g., exhibitions with technology, digitization with curriculum development) and describe how resources will be allocated across activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of partnerships and leveraging of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees commonly leveraged grant resources through partnerships with individuals and institutions as part of project implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly three-quarters of surveyed museums reported partnerships as part of project implementation. Applications should describe partner roles, leveraged resources, and collaboration plans as part of project design and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission/resubmitting unfunded projects within same category allowed and can improve success
rubrics_metrics.description: Museums may revise and resubmit unfunded applications; resubmissions to the same grant category are common and can increase funding likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data indicate about 25% of institutions resubmitted an unfunded project to the same category; roughly one-third of those resubmissions were ultimately funded. Collections Stewardship resubmissions had particularly high success (more than half funded after two or three tries). Applicants should consider feedback, revise proposals, and may reapply within the same category if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration (typical timeframe observed)
rubrics_metrics.description: MFA projects in the sample lasted one, two, or three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning, applicants should propose realistic timelines consistent with project scope; the evaluation sample focused on first completed projects that fell into 1–3 year durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award size categories and association with project types
rubrics_metrics.description: Award amounts are commonly grouped (small < $50,000; medium $50,000–$99,000; large ≥ $100,000) and are associated with different project emphases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming projects were associated more frequently with larger awards (≥ $100,000). Applicants should match proposed scope to realistic award-size expectations and justify budget requests relative to project activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observed applicant/institutional characteristics that affect funding patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation findings show patterns in funding likelihood associated with institutional characteristics and applicant behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed patterns: institutions with larger annual operating budgets were more likely to receive MFA awards; repeat applicants had higher award rates (award rates increased with the number of application attempts); regional and discipline distributions affect application patterns (e.g., New England had more history museums and higher reapplication rates). Applicants should be aware that institutional capacity and experience with applications correlate with funding outcomes and should address capacity-building elements in proposals if relevant.
